text:
Alex G: Quick FYI - saw duplicated side-effects in sampleapp when a 429 landed right as OIDC refresh finished. Tiny repro and an idea below.

Alex G: Repro steps:
1) client sends op O (user action)
2) server returns 429
3) SDK fires the normal retry path (short backoff)
4) auth refresh finishes -> SDK replays original logical op -> server ends up processing two independent requests

Alex G: Minimal log snippet:
```
POST /v1/generate -> 429
[auth] refresh: started
retry#1 -> send (no replay header)
[auth] refresh: finished
original: re-emit -> send (no replay header)
```

Sophie M: Ugh. Do we have any per-operation stable id by default? If not, servers can't dedupe. Some examples add headers manually but it's ad-hoc.

Rafael T: Agreed. Parity gap across languages. Also streaming requests complicate things. We should default to non-replayable for streams unless user opts in.

Alex G: Proposal (sketch): introduce a tiny client-side feature set named "replay-safeguard":
- generate a short opaque header `Replay-Ticket: <base62>` at request build time and persist it across retries and refresh flows
- attach a per-client refresh-lock: if a refresh is in-flight, new retries for ops that started before the refresh are gated until either refresh completes or an adaptive backoff window passes
- keep a small in-memory client-side dedupe set of recently emitted Replay-Tickets so the client won't resend a ticket twice if it already re-emitted it after a race
- streaming ops default to replayable=false; expose `replayable: true` explicitly

Sophie M: Nice. How does the refresh-lock work? If refresh blocks retries we might add latency. We need to minimize extra tail.

Alex G: Idea: refresh-lock only gates retries for ops that started earlier than the refresh-start time. For new ops started after refresh completes, normal behavior. When refresh is in-flight, first retry delay = max(backoff, refreshEstimateMs * 0.7) + jitter. That biases retries to land after refresh without waiting full refresh sometimes.

Rafael T: Two more ideas: 1) allow server-side capability discovery (Accepts-Replay header) so sampleapp can handshake; 2) add a lightweight client dedupe TTL (e.g., keep tickets 30s) so if the SDK re-emits a ticket we can avoid duplicate sends locally. Servers still need dedupe but client dedupe reduces noise.

Sophie M: Server capability discovery is optional but useful for progressive rollout. If server responds Accepts-Replay: true, client can enable conservative replay mode automatically in onboarding sampleapp. Nice UX.

Alex G: Example middleware pseudo:
```js
// sdk-core replay-safeguard middleware
function replaySafeguard(next, ctx) {
  if (!ctx.request.replayable) return next();
  const ticket = ctx.request.headers['Replay-Ticket'] || genTicket();
  ctx.request.headers['Replay-Ticket'] = ticket;
  // gate if refresh in-flight and op started before refreshStart
  if (client.isRefreshInFlight() && ctx.request.startedAt < client.refreshStartTs) {
     const delay = Math.max(ctx.backoffMs, Math.floor(client.estimatedRefreshMs * 0.7)) + jitter();
     await sleep(delay);
  }
  // de-duplicate locally - if we already sent this ticket recently skip re-send
  if (client.localSentTickets.has(ticket)) return client.localSentResponse(ticket);
  client.localSentTickets.add(ticket);
  return next();
}
```

Rafael T: Testing plan: unit tests for middleware logic + e2e that simulates 429 + refresh taking X ms. Assert server-side only saw one unique Replay-Ticket when server honors header. Also test fallback where server ignores header: client avoids hammering via gate & budget.

Sophie M: Telemetry we should emit: replay.ticket_generated, replay.retry_blocked_by_refresh, replay.sent_after_refresh, replay.local_dedup_hit, replay.server_dedup_observed. That helps measure both server adoption and client-side effectiveness.

Alex G: UX for sampleapp: add `conservativeReplayOnboarding: true` that enables replay-safeguard + server dedupe demo. Show server snippet that uses a tiny TTL cache for Replay-Tickets. Recommend TTL = clamp(estimatedProcMs*2, 1000, 30000).

Rafael T: Edge cases: token rotation across multiple client instances (e.g., serverless) means client dedupe can't be relied on alone; server dedupe is required for correctness. Document that clearly.

Sophie M: Also note we should not auto-enable replay-safeguard for production clients until servers widely honor Replay-Ticket; onboarding mode only by default.

replay-checker-bot: (automated) Created DEVTICKET-930: "replay-safeguard: Replay-Ticket header + refresh-lock gating + client dedupe cache + Accepts-Replay handshake + telemetry + e2e tests"

Alex G: I'll draft a short spec and Node PR for the middleware and a sampleapp server demo. Can someone pick up Go/Python parity check?

Rafael T: I'll take Go and coordinate telemetry names.

Sophie M: I'll draft the sampleapp README blurb and the server TTL guidance. Add to SDK sync agenda. :calendar:
